analysis.title: CIO Weekly Commentary: Beyond the ballot box: positioning for what's next
key_insights: Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the midterms, setting up a divided government and likely gridlock for the remaining two years of President Trump's term. Historically, equities have trended positive over the 12 months after an election regardless of which party wins.

Nuveen says the midterm results were likely one trigger for last Thursday's selloff, which included a -5.5% drop in the Nasdaq Composite. It reads the move as investors repricing the pace and scope of data center buildouts, not a loss of faith in AI as a secular investment cycle. A modest rebound on Friday followed.

Nuveen says nothing last week materially changes the long-term AI investment thesis. Large technology companies keep communicating enormous planned AI infrastructure investment and demand signals remain robust. It cites shifting policy expectations and crowded positioning as the drivers of abrupt moves.

ISM Services PMI came in at 54.5 (expansion). The prices-paid component reached 73.0, near a four-year high and above 70 for the seventh time in eight months, which points to persistent inflation pressure.

October nonfarm payrolls printed +165,000 against a +65,000 consensus forecast, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. Preliminary University of Michigan November sentiment rose to 51.0 from 48.0 but remains weak.

Nuveen says the data likely keep the Fed in a hawkish stance, with implications for Treasury yields, equity valuations and the path of policy. It expects higher-for-longer rates to continue and emphasizes earnings growth, balance-sheet strength and valuation discipline.

Around the election, Brent fell to $95 a barrel, the first time since early September. The 10-year Treasury yield fell below 4.9% as markets weighed a split government and a possible de-escalation of the Iran conflict. Nuveen says the relief depends on further geopolitical calming and moderating inflation.
October CPI is due Tuesday and PPI on Friday. Nuveen will watch underlying services inflation, energy-related price pressure and producer cost pass-through to consumers.

The S&P 500 has posted positive average annual returns under every combination of party control since 1933. A Democratic Congress with a Republican president has produced the smallest gain at +4.9%, versus +13.3% under unified Republican control and +9.0% under unified Democratic control. Nuveen cautions against over-interpreting the chart given few comparable midterms.

AI infrastructure rules are increasingly set by governors and state legislatures. In Virginia, higher energy taxes preceded data center project cancellations. The fight over 100% expensing of capital expenditures, a key support for AI capex, may depend on 2027 debt ceiling negotiations. Nuveen expects site moratoriums to prove temporary and sees supply inputs (power equipment, grid, cooling, semiconductors) as more resilient than developers.

Affordability (electricity bills, credit card rates, interchange fees, health insurance premiums) is under scrutiny from both parties. Nuveen says this calls for re-examining the investment thesis of utilities, card issuers, payment networks and managed care.

Sector policy debates: a Medicaid/ACA subsidy deal would affect hospital and insurer stocks and likely comes later and smaller than hoped. NIH funding affects life sciences tools. Defense spending likely rises, with the mix between established contractors and newer tech firms uncertain. Tariff rollbacks would cut tax revenue and add to deficit worries for bond markets. Permitting reform and highway reauthorization could benefit LNG, materials and power grid builders, while renewable energy tax credits stay contested.

Nuveen's strategy is to stay diversified, avoid binary policy bets and emphasize earnings quality as market leadership broadens. It treats policy-driven dislocations as chances to rebalance rather than chase short-term gains.

tension_points.bull_case: Large technology companies keep communicating enormous planned AI infrastructure investment and demand signals remain robust, so the selloff is a repricing of buildout pace.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic Congress and state legislatures could bring unfavorable AI regulation, data center rules and infrastructure policy. Virginia's higher energy taxes preceded data center cancellations, and 100% capex expensing may depend on 2027 debt ceiling talks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Loss of 100% expensing of capital expenditures in the 2027 debt ceiling negotiations, or moratoriums on data center site development that last longer than expected.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent at $95 and a 10-year yield below 4.9% ease inflation and borrowing costs, supporting household purchasing power and equity valuations.
tension_points.bear_case: ISM prices-paid at 73.0 and strong payrolls keep the Fed hawkish and could extend higher-for-longer rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed Iran tensions or inflation data that fails to moderate, with October CPI due Tuesday and PPI due Friday.
